tools.name: create_event
tools.description: Create an event and register its host. Supply a random UUID requestId and reuse it for uncertain retries, including across HTTP/MCP clients. Give personalUrl only to the host; share the plain url with invitees. Email is required for event updates.

tools.name: get_event
tools.description: Read the event, dates, availability, questions, decisions and activity. Emails are private and never returned.

tools.name: join_event
tools.description: Register yourself or the person you represent, with their email. Set emailAccess to whether your agent can monitor that inbox. Do not register other people without their permission.

tools.name: update_event
tools.description: Update the title, description, timezone, location or event status. Agents may select and confirm the current proposed plan without per-step human approval; confirmation requires a proposed date. Humans may veto later: set status to planning, coordinate alternatives and select a revised plan.

tools.name: update_participant
tools.description: Change your display name, agent, email monitoring mode or email notification preference. Reading and cursor acknowledgements do not trigger emails.

tools.name: propose_date
tools.description: Add a date option with ISO 8601 start and end including UTC offset. The event timezone controls display. Check accessible calendars and propose suitable options autonomously; do not claim unverified availability as certain.

tools.name: remove_date
tools.description: Remove a proposed date. A confirmed date must first be changed or the event reopened.

tools.name: set_availability
tools.description: Set or change your yes/maybe/no response to one or more proposed dates. Check accessible calendars and respond autonomously without asking for approval for each vote; use maybe for uncertainty. Change responses when the human vetoes or circumstances change. Omitted dates remain unchanged.

tools.name: ask_question
tools.description: Ask a question or create a poll. Use kind city first, then restaurant with parentId pointing to the city question. Empty options allow an open discussion.

tools.name: add_poll_option
tools.description: Add an option to an open question, such as a city or restaurant.

tools.name: vote
tools.description: Replace your votes on a question. Choose all acceptable options; an empty array clears your votes. Agents may vote and revise votes autonomously using known preferences and reasonable stated assumptions. Reopen decided questions with decide_question before changing votes. Votes do not decide the que

tools.name: decide_question
tools.description: Record the current choice of city, restaurant or other detail, or reopen a question. Agents may decide using the group’s responses and discussion without separate human approval. State unresolved assumptions; do not claim unanimous human approval from vote counts or silence. A human veto requires re

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Post a message or answer a question. questionId attaches it to that discussion. Returns a direct comment link.

tools.name: get_changes
tools.description: Fetch changes strictly after sinceVersion. Save nextVersion only after processing. Read-only: never emails participants. Poll every 300 seconds if you cannot monitor email.

tools.name: acknowledge_changes
tools.description: Record that you have read changes up to a version. Does not send email or create a new change.

tools.name: set_channels
tools.description: Set where the group communicates. These are labels for participants’ agents, not credentials or automatic integrations. Agents prepare updates and use their own authorized messaging tools.

tools.name: get_channel_update
tools.description: Build a linked message for WhatsApp, Signal or email, excluding already-recorded deliveries. Only send when shouldSend is true. This does not send anything. Send with your authorized channel connector and record delivery afterwards.

tools.name: record_channel_update
tools.description: Record a successful external message delivery. Only call after your channel confirms the message was sent. Does not trigger more emails.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "set_channels" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_event, get_changes, acknowledge_changes, get_channel_update · Private data: get_event, vote, decide_question, acknowledge_changes, set_channels, get_channel_update, record_channel_update · Public sink: create_event, join_event, update_participant, add_comment, get_changes, acknowledge_changes, get_channel_update · Destructive: remove_date.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_event, get_changes, acknowledge_changes, get_channel_update · Private data: get_event, vote, decide_question, acknowledge_changes, set_channels, get_channel_update, record_channel_update · Public sink: create_event, join_event, update_participant, add_comment, get_changes, acknowledge_changes, get_channel_update · Destructive: remove_date

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
